#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);

result.builder:
Goal: one pull request that adds a --shout flag to greet-cli and meets every line of issue.expect.

Context: bin/greet.js takes the first argument that does not start with `--` as the name and prints `${greeting(name)}\n`, where src/greet.js exports `greeting = (name) => `Hello, ${name}!``. Tests are in test/greet.test.js and run with `npm test` (node --test). .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes the docs/ directory to GitHub Pages on push to main, so docs/index.md is the source of the published page.

Steps:
1. In bin/greet.js, detect `--shout` among process.argv.slice(2) (in any position relative to the name). When present, print the greeting in upper case, e.g. `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline. Keep name parsing as it is, so `--shout` is never taken as the name. You may add a helper in src/greet.js (e.g. a shout option or function), but do not change what `greeting(name)` returns.
2. Without --shout, the output must stay exactly as today: `node bin/greet.js Ada` prints `Hello, Ada!\n`; with no name it still writes `usage: greet <name>` to stderr and exits 2. You may mention --shout in the usage text only if the no-name behaviour (stderr, exit code 2) is otherwise unchanged; simplest is to leave it alone.
3. Update docs/index.md to document --shout: show the usage `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and state that it prints the greeting in upper case (e.g. `HELLO, <NAME>!`). Keep it in docs/index.md so the existing pages workflow publishes it; do not change .github/workflows/pages.yml.
4. Add tests to test/greet.test.js: one that runs `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and expects `HELLO, ADA!\n`, and keep the existing tests that check unchanged output without the flag.
5. Run `npm test` and confirm all tests pass, then open the pull request. In the PR description, note that the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ will only list --shout after merge, when the pages workflow deploys docs/.

Check 1 — expect: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
Run: `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`, and also `node bin/greet.js Ada` to get the normal greeting.
PASS: each --shout run exits 0 and its stdout equals the upper-case form of the normal greeting for the same name (for the current greeting, `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline).
FAIL: either --shout run exits non-zero, prints the usage message, prints the greeting not in upper case, or prints something other than the upper-cased greeting.

Check 2 — expect: "without --shout the output is unchanged"
Run: at the head, `node bin/greet.js Ada; echo "exit=$?"` and `node bin/greet.js; echo "exit=$?"` (capture stdout and stderr separately). Then get the same outputs from the code before the change (e.g. `git stash`-free: `git worktree add /tmp/greet-base <merge-base of the PR>` or `git show <merge-base>:bin/greet.js` with its src) and compare. Also run `npm test` at the head.
PASS: `node bin/greet.js Ada` prints exactly `Hello, Ada!\n` with exit 0, the no-name run behaves the same as before the change (stdout, stderr and exit code 2 match the base), and `npm test` passes.
FAIL: any output or exit code differs from the base when --shout is not given, or `npm test` fails.

Check 3 — expect: "docs/index.md documents --shout"
Read: docs/index.md at the head.
PASS: the file mentions `--shout` and says what it does (prints the greeting in upper case).
FAIL: docs/index.md does not mention --shout, or mentions it without saying what it does.

Check 4 — expect: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"
The live page can only be seen after merge; do not fetch it. Check what the head contains that will produce it. Read: .github/workflows/pages.yml and docs/index.md at the head.
PASS: .github/workflows/pages.yml still runs on push to main and uploads the `docs` directory as the Pages artifact and deploys it, and docs/index.md at the head lists --shout (so the published page will list it once merged).
FAIL: the workflow no longer publishes docs/ on push to main (removed, path changed, trigger changed), or docs/index.md at the head does not list --shout.

Advisory
- Check test/greet.test.js has a test for the --shout output; its absence is worth noting but is not a FAIL.
- Note whether --shout works when placed before and after the name; both are covered in Check 1.
- Note any change to what `greeting(name)` in src/greet.js returns.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #12 (the `--shout` flag) and the harness accepted them. I made no changes to the repo.

**Builder brief:** add `--shout` in `bin/greet.js` so that `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`. It also says to:
- leave the output without the flag exactly as it is;
- document the flag in `docs/index.md`;
- add a CLI test for it;
- run `npm test`.

It tells the builder not to touch `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, the workflow that publishes `docs/` when changes are pushed to `main`.

**Verifier brief:** one check per expect line, in the issue's order:
1. **Upper case:** run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`. PASS if both print the normal greeting in upper case.
2. **Unchanged without the flag:** compare the output and exit codes with the code before the change, for both a name and no name, and run `npm test`.
3. **Docs:** read `docs/index.md` at the PR head. PASS if it names `--shout` and says what it does.
4. **Published page:** the live page can only be seen after merge, so the check doesn't fetch it. Instead it confirms the pages workflow still publishes `docs/` on push to `main` and that `docs/index.md` lists `--shout`.

Anything stricter, like requiring a test for the flag, is listed under an Advisory heading and isn't a pass or fail condition.

**Wording slip in check 2:** it calls the step for getting the pre-change output "`git stash`-free". That phrase is muddled, though the method it gives (a separate worktree at the merge base, or `git show`) is still clear.
